newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish Life buys U.S. firm for $163 mln.
newsitem.headline: Irish Life buys U.S. firm for $163 mln.

text.p: Irish Life Plc said on Thursday its U.S. unit Irish Life of North America had agreed to buy the Guarantee Reserve Life Insurance Co for $163 million.
Irish Life said the acquisition of the privately-owned U.S. firm would be funded from its existing resources and from debt financing. The acquisition would enhance earnings, it said.
Managing director David Kingston said in a statement the acquisition represented a significant further development of its U.S. business and would have a major beneficial impact on the group.
He called it "a very successful company in its target market" which would add an innovative distribution channel and open up opportunities for growth at its existing U.S. businesses.
Irish Life said it estimated the embedded value of Guarantee Reserve would be $146 million at end-March 1997, the expected completion date of the transaction.
It said the U.S. company was licensed to write life assurance and accidental and health business in 47 states plus Washington DC. It has 175 employees and around 340,000 policyholders.
"The company's product and market focus is on providing risk benefits to older age groups," Irish Life said.

It said Guarantee Reserve had total admitted assets of $188.2 million and capital and surplus of $44.0 million at end-1995. Premium income and new business were $81.8 million and $25.2 million respectively in 1995, it said.
Guarantee Reserve's statutory profit before tax and net realised capital gains was $9.5 million in 1995, while premium income for the six months to June 1996 was $46.1 million, Irish Life said.
